purpose: Calibration anchors for the king-tide toggle and the 'has this already happened' reality check. Converted to NAVD88 using the station's NAVD88 offset of 12.15 ft above station datum.

anchors.name: MHHW
anchors.note: Mean higher-high water, 1983-2001 epoch. Baseline for the SLR slider.

anchors.name: HAT
anchors.note: Highest astronomical tide. The honest value for a king-tide toggle - an earlier draft assumed +1.5 ft above MHHW, which is ~0.5 ft too aggressive for astronomy alone.

anchors.name: Observed maximum water level
anchors.note: Hurricane Irma storm surge. A 'this already happened' marker - NOAA Intermediate does not reach this as a daily high tide until roughly 2100.

noaa_flood_thresholds_ft_NAVD88.note: Major flooding has never been recorded at this gauge. NOAA Intermediate projects 70 days/yr by 2100.

tide_range.note: A ~2 ft range means MHHW vs MSL differs by ~1.1 ft - comparable to 45 years of Intermediate SLR. State which tidal stage every scenario assumes.
